entities.summary:
Nebdjefara, a pharaoh of the Fourteenth Dynasty of Egypt, ruled for 12 to 24 months during the 17th century BC, leaving behind a severely damaged Turin King List as his sole source of information.

This brief yet pivotal reign had a lasting impact on ancient Egyptian history, as it marked a transitional period between the New Kingdom and the Second Intermediate Period.

Nebdjefara's significance extends beyond his own rule, as it highlights the fragility and impermanence of even the most powerful dynasties. His story serves as a reminder that even the smallest actions can have far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of human civilization in profound ways.

Like a fleeting moment in time, Nebdjefara's reign has left an indelible mark on our understanding of ancient Egypt, a testament to the enduring power of history to captivate and inspire us.
